sections.content: You know *cuyo* from B1 Unit 5: it links a person or thing to something that belongs to it, and it means "whose". It agrees with the noun that comes after it (*cuyo gobierno*, *cuya constitución*, *cuyos jefes*, *cuyas leyes*), not with the owner. It is a good tool for comparing Cárdenas in Mexico with Vargas in Brazil.

items.spanish: Cárdenas fue un presidente cuyo gobierno repartió tierras a los campesinos.
items.english: Cárdenas was a president whose government gave land to the peasants.

items.spanish: México era un país cuya constitución no permitía la reelección.
items.english: Mexico was a country whose constitution did not allow re-election.

items.spanish: Vargas fue un presidente cuyas leyes protegieron a los trabajadores.
items.english: Vargas was a president whose laws protected the workers.

items.spanish: Los campesinos cuyas familias recibieron tierras formaron ejidos.
items.english: The peasants whose families received land formed ejidos.

sections.content: Never put an article between *cuyo* and its noun: *cuyo gobierno*, not *cuyo el gobierno*. Do not replace it with *que su*: *un presidente que su gobierno…* is a common mistake.
